findings.text: Affinity change notification can be installed, replaced or cleared for a given interrupt number. Installation completes the supplied object with identity, lifetime tracking and deferred work; clearing is done by passing an empty registration. Replacement is atomic and the previous object has its pending work cancelled and its lifetime released. Missing descriptors and NMI lines are refused.

Provides nonblocking disable, hard disable with synchronization, and NMI named aliases for disable and enable. Nonblocking forms return promptly without waiting for in flight handlers, while the hard form additionally waits when a disable actually took effect and reports whether waiting occurred. NMI named forms delegate directly to the generic paths.

Wake capability is managed through a counted interface where repeated enables nest and only the outermost transition touches hardware. The initial enable programs the chip and records wakeup state, the final disable reverses both, and a hardware failure restores the prior count. Chips that declare wake programming unnecessary succeed trivially, chips without wake support report absence of hardware, and NMI lines are rejected.

Exposes queries and small setters for interrupt descriptors. Request eligibility checks global validity, request permission and either absence of handlers or compatible shared use. Parent linkage records a parent number under protection. Presence of handlers and masked status bits can be tested safely under read side protection without taking the descriptor lock, returning a simple boolean.

Per CPU interrupts are requested with a handler, name, affinity and per CPU identity. Creation supplies defaults when affinity is absent, marks the handler as per CPU and suspend insensitive, and permits sharing only when the mask does not cover every CPU. Requests validate descriptor presence, request permission and per CPU nature, and for NMI variants additionally require autoenable off, chip NMI support and no conflicting full mask NMI already present.

Per CPU lines have explicit per CPU enable, disable, liveness test, teardown and NMI delivery preparation. Enable honors a caller supplied trigger sense or falls back to the recorded default and then enables on the current CPU. Disable and test operate on the current CPU only. Freeing unlinks the matching per CPU identity under protection, refuses to free while still enabled on overlapping CPUs, and clears NMI state when the last handler departs.

Non maskable interrupts are requested and freed as exclusive per CPU lines with chip assistance. Requests reject disconnected numbers, shared or suspend or poll flags, non per CPU use, missing handlers, autoenable mismatches and chips without NMI capability. Successful setup records NMI state and invokes chip preparation, with failure triggering full cleanup. Freeing ensures the line is disabled, tears down chip state and releases resources.

Threaded handling exposes explicit wakeup for a handler thread selected by device identity, plus internal readiness signalling and secondary chaining. Wakeup by device identity looks up the descriptor, rejects per CPU device lines, and wakes the matching thread if one exists. Readiness marks a thread ready and wakes waiters for thread startup. Secondary chaining validates the secondary link and wakes it under protection.

Affinity notifier lifetime is reference counted across replacement and deferred execution. Each installed object holds a reference that is dropped on replacement alongside cancellation of pending work, with an extra drop when cancellation succeeds because pending work held its own reference. The deferred worker always drops a reference on completion, even when the descriptor is missing or temporary mask allocation fails.

NMI use is allowed only for directly managed lines on chips that explicitly declare NMI support and do not sit behind a slow bus interface. Hierarchical lines with a parent are excluded. Setup without chip hooks is treated as invalid while teardown without hooks is a no operation.

Per CPU handler objects carry fixed attributes regardless of caller flags. They are always per CPU and suspend insensitive, retain the supplied handler, name, affinity and per CPU identity, and gain a shared marking exactly when the effective affinity excludes at least one possible CPU. A missing affinity defaults to all possible CPUs, which therefore never gains the shared marking from this rule.

Thread affinity adaptation is conditional on build configuration and on a per handler flag. One configuration provides an empty operation, the other clears the flag, snapshots the effective affinity under protection, and applies it to the current thread. If temporary mask storage cannot be obtained, the flag is restored so the attempt repeats later, and the thread state is made runnable before the attempt.

Handler presence and status bit tests are safe without descriptor locking by holding read side protection across descriptor lookup and field access. Absent descriptors yield negative answers, and status testing masks the accessor protected status word with the caller supplied bit selection.

A per descriptor spinlock with interrupt protection guards notifier replacement, affinity and effective affinity snapshots, oneshot thread mask updates, thread wake selection, NMI state changes and handler list unlinking. Holders keep critical sections short, never invoke callbacks or sleep while holding it, and use scoped forms that also save interrupt state where the caller may run with interrupts enabled.

A per descriptor chip bus lock serializes sequences that may program the chip against concurrent chip access. Oneshot completion holds it across the whole retry and unmask decision, per CPU freeing holds it while unlinking and releasing, and wake transitions acquire it together with descriptor lookup. It is always released through a synchronizing unlock that flushes pending chip operations.

Descriptor lookup and locking are combined in scoped helpers that validate global versus per CPU expectations and fail cleanly with an invalid indicator when the descriptor is absent or of the wrong class. Global helpers are used for wake, request eligibility and parent updates, while per CPU helpers gate enable, liveness, disable and NMI preparation. Failure paths never touch descriptor fields.

Per CPU allocation state groups counters for total and managed capacity and usage, boolean conditions for initialization and online status, and bitmap areas for general allocation and managed reservation. The managed bitmap is placed directly after the allocation bitmap in a trailing flexible area, so each per CPU instance owns a contiguous pair of equal sized maps.

Global vector matrix state groups bit width, allocation window bounds and size, global availability and reservation counts, system bits excluded from allocation, total allocated count and online map count, plus a per CPU pointer to per CPU state, a system wide bitmap and a scratch area. The scratch area is a trailing flexible array sized to twice the bitmap length, with the second half serving as the system map.

Interrupt descriptors observed here coordinate affinity, wake counting, threading, NMI marking and per CPU state. They carry a lock, a notifier pointer, common affinity, wake depth, oneshot and in progress state, a thread oneshot mask, a handler chain head, a parent number, a per CPU enable mask and a wait queue for thread startup. Handler objects carry interrupt number, handler and thread callbacks, flags, names, device identities, affinity, thread task, thread mask and thread flags, plus a secondary link.

Each threaded handler runs a dedicated kernel thread that signals readiness, selects scheduling class and handler flavor, installs exit cleanup, then loops waiting for work. Waiting is interruptible and honors stop requests, with a final run if work was pending at stop time. Each wake runs either the regular or forced thread path, optionally chains to a secondary on a wake request outcome, and then wakes thread waiters.

Oneshot completion runs after each threaded invocation except for lines without oneshot marking or for forced secondary handlers. It retries while the line reports in progress elsewhere, aborts unmasking if new thread work arrived meanwhile, clears the calling thread bit from the shared oneshot mask, and unmasks the line only when no thread bits remain and the line is enabled but masked. All decisions occur under combined bus and spin protection.

Wake and NMI states evolve through counted and flagged transitions. Wake depth starts empty, increments on enable and decrements on disable, with hardware programming only on transitions away from and back to empty. NMI marking is set after successful handler installation and chip preparation, and cleared when the last handler is removed or during explicit cleanup and teardown. Preparation must precede use on each CPU and teardown follows, both requiring non preemptible context.

Three fixed primary and secondary entry targets cover default threading and misuse detection for nested lines and forced secondary dispatch. The default primary unconditionally requests thread wakeup. The nested primary and forced secondary warn about unexpected invocation and report no handling, serving as placeholders that surface configuration errors.

Matrix creation is an early initialization entry that builds global and per CPU allocation state for a given bit width and window. It allocates the global object with room for scratch and system maps, records dimensions and window, allocates per CPU storage, and links each per CPU managed view to the second half of its local maps. Any allocation failure yields a null result with prior partial allocation released.

Misuse is detected through warnings rather than silent corruption. Unbalanced wake disable, freeing an already free or still enabled per CPU line, freeing from interrupt context, freeing a non NMI line as NMI, calling the primary for a nested line, invoking a secondary placeholder, exiting while still an active thread, waking a missing secondary, and preparing NMI on a non NMI line all warn. Most continue with a safe fallback such as refusing the operation or cleaning up partial state.

Races and resource shortages have explicit handling. Oneshot completion waits with relaxation while another CPU holds in progress, preventing permanent masking when the thread outruns the hard handler. Affinity notification and thread migration tolerate temporary mask allocation failure by skipping notification or retrying later. Matrix creation tolerates global or per CPU allocation failure by returning null without leaking.

Handler outcomes use distinct named results: IRQ_WAKE_THREAD requests threaded execution, IRQ_NONE reports that the line was not serviced, and IRQ_HANDLED records a per descriptor handled count when returned from threaded execution.

Failures use conventional negative indicators: EINVAL covers bad numbers and forbidden combinations and wrong class and NMI misuse and preemptible preparation, ENOMEM covers allocation failure, ENXIO covers absent wake support when not skippable, and ENOTCONN covers an explicitly unconnected number.

Request and control flags use named bits such as IRQF_SHARED and IRQF_PERCPU and IRQF_NO_THREAD and IRQF_NOBALANCING and IRQF_NO_SUSPEND and IRQF_NO_AUTOEN and IRQF_COND_SUSPEND and IRQF_IRQPOLL and IRQ_TYPE_NONE with a sense mask. NMI requests forbid the shared and conditional suspend and poll bits while requiring the per CPU bit. Per CPU creation always adds per CPU and no suspend.
